interface.title: Functional Scoliosis Assessment
interface.field: Biomechanics / clinical movement science (markerless motion capture for scoliosis screening)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and reproduction of a published study: processing recorded joint-tracking trials into asymmetry tables, plots and a screening summary
interface.what_it_is_for: Turns recorded skeleton-tracking trials (Kinect, MediaPipe or offline JSON/CSV dumps) into shoulder and hip angle asymmetry measures (RS_θ, LS_θ, Δθs, RH_θ, LH_θ, Δθh) for static standing and dynamic walking, with time-domain and STFT plots and a summary that separates healthy-like from elevated asymmetry, either for a batch of subjects or for one subject.

data.note: The 'Generate paper-style sample Subjects 1–3' button wrote synthetic sample trials to /work/app/data/samples_compact, and the batch pipeline ran on that folder. No test files were available for upload (browser_list_files returned an empty list), so the Single subject report was built with no trial files and every angle came out as NaN. The reviewer notes that the repo ships per-subject trial files (data/samples_compact/subject_01/*.json: static_trial_1/2, dynamic_trial_1/2, sitting_trial_1) that could be uploaded in a new run.

tree.general: Measure left/right body asymmetry from recorded movement trials to screen for deformity-related patterns and reproduce a published study's results
tree.specific: Reproduce the Kinect scoliosis screening paper's static and dynamic shoulder/hip angle tables, time and STFT plots, and inference summary

features.name: Protocol-conformance checklist with live warnings
features.general: Enter the recording conditions next to the reference protocol; a warning appears for each checked condition that differs and clears once it is fixed
features.specific: Sidebar Study setup checklist: Distance to camera (paper 2.5 m), Tight dark clothing, Closed room / no strong sunlight, Camera height adjusted; each mismatch shows a yellow note (e.g. 'Subject distance 1.0 m differs from paper 2.5 m', 'Paper recommends tight dark clothing to reduce joint flicker'). An optional Treadmill speed field is also present but never triggers a warning (0.10 and 3.0 both tried)
steps: Type or step the camera distance
Tick or untick each environment condition
Optionally set treadmill speed (not checked against the protocol)
Read the warnings and correct the setup until they clear
serves_tasks: Check the recording setup against the protocol and see warnings where it differs

features.name: Batch dataset runner (sample generator + folder-in/folder-out pipeline)
features.general: Optionally generate an example dataset, point the tool at an input folder and an output folder, and run the whole analysis over every subject in one go
features.specific: Batch dataset tab: Generate paper-style sample Subjects 1–3 → Dataset folder / Output folder text boxes → Run study pipeline → 'Processed 3 subjects' followed by the summary, tables and plots
steps: Press Generate paper-style sample Subjects 1–3 (optional; shows 'Wrote samples to …')
Check or edit Dataset folder
Check or edit Output folder
Press Run study pipeline and wait (several minutes) for 'Processed N subjects'
serves_tasks: Create an example dataset to work with
Run the analysis over every subject and read the per-subject screening summary

features.name: Bilateral joint-angle asymmetry tables (static vs dynamic)
features.general: Tables with one row per subject giving left and right joint angles and the difference between them, one table for a standing trial and one for a walking trial, so asymmetry can be compared across subjects and conditions
features.specific: Two uncaptioned tables, static then dynamic (the paper's Tables 3 and 4), with columns Subject, RS_θ, LS_θ, Δθs, RH_θ, LH_θ, Δθh; e.g. Subject 2's Δθs goes from 2.51 static to 7.15 dynamic
steps: Run the pipeline
Read Δθs/Δθh for each subject in the static table
Compare against the same columns in the dynamic table
serves_tasks: Compare joint-angle asymmetry across subjects in standing and walking

features.name: Rule-based screening summary
features.general: A text summary that turns the asymmetry numbers into a plain-language pattern label for each subject, gives the change from standing to walking, and ranks subjects, with a disclaimer that it is not a diagnosis
features.specific: Inference summary (research/screening aid — not a clinical diagnosis): for each subject, history, Static and Dynamic Δθs/Δθh, a Pattern note (mild / elevated dynamic asymmetry / healthy-like) and the Dynamic−static Δθs change, plus a cross-subject line naming the lowest and highest dynamic shoulder deviation. Verified through the batch pipeline only; on the single-subject route with no input it still labels NaN values 'mild asymmetry'
steps: Run the batch pipeline (or build a single-subject report)
Read each subject's static and dynamic deltas
Read the pattern note and the dynamic−static change
Read the cross-subject ranking
serves_tasks: Run the analysis over every subject and read the per-subject screening summary
Enter the subject's demographics and trial files, then generate their report

features.name: Time-domain and STFT joint-angle panels
features.general: Side-by-side figures of each joint's angle over a trial (with trend lines) and its short-time Fourier spectrogram, one panel per joint, to judge how asymmetry and rhythm change over time
features.specific: 'Time domain — Subject 1 (dynamic)' and 'STFT — Subject 1 (dynamic)' figures, each with Right Shoulder, Left Shoulder, Right Hip and Left Hip panels
steps: Run the pipeline
Scroll to the Time domain figure and compare left and right trend lines
Compare with the STFT spectrograms for the same joints
serves_tasks: Look at how joint angles change over a walking trial in time and frequency
